lessons.title: WRITE and the I Format
intro: WRITE (6,10) A, B prints A and B. The 6 is the unit number of the line printer, the 10 is the label of the FORMAT card that describes the line.
In the FORMAT, I5 means: an integer, right-aligned in 5 columns. 42 with I5 becomes three spaces and 42. If the number doesn't fit, the printer prints stars: *****.

One more rule from the line printer: the first character of every line is a control code and isn't printed. A blank means "normal line". That's why FORMATs start with 1X (one blank) or a text starting with a blank.

exercises.prompt: What does the 6 in WRITE (6,10) mean?
exercises.explanation: Unit 6 was the line printer on most systems. Unit 5 was the card reader.
I5 right-aligns the integer in five columns.

exercises.prompt: What happens when you print 123 with I2?
exercises.explanation: If the number doesn't fit, FORTRAN prints stars, so you notice.

options: The first character is a control code for the printer and isn't printed
The H is a FORTRAN keyword
Text is always cut by one letter
exercises.explanation: The H is taken as a control character. Write ' HELLO' or start the FORMAT with 1X.

exercises.prompt: Print the integer K right-aligned in 4 columns.
exercises.explanation: I for integer, then the width.

exercises.prompt: What does 1X do at the start of a FORMAT?
options: Prints one blank, which the printer uses as its control code
exercises.explanation: 1X is one blank space. As the first character it means "normal line".

lessons.title: The F Format
intro: REAL numbers are printed with Fw.d: w columns in total, with d digits after the decimal point. F6.2 prints 3.14159 as two blanks and 3.14.
The width counts everything: the sign, the digits and the point. The value is rounded to d decimals.
Integers need I, reals need F. Mixing them up stops the job with *ERROR*.

exercises.explanation: Two decimals, rounded, right-aligned in 6 columns.

exercises.prompt: What does the 2 in F6.2 mean?
options: Two digits after the decimal point
exercises.explanation: Fw.d: w is the width, d the number of decimals.
1234.5 has 6 characters. It doesn't fit into 5, so: stars.

exercises.prompt: Print the REAL X with two decimals in 8 columns.
This job stops with *ERROR*. Which card is wrong?
exercises.explanation: X is REAL, but I5 is for integers. Use F5.1 or similar.

lessons.title: Text, Spaces and New Lines
intro: A FORMAT can mix text and values: FORMAT (' AREA =', F8.2) prints a label and a number on one line. Text goes into the FORMAT, not the WRITE.
nX prints n blanks, and / starts a new line. The original FORTRAN wrote text as nH followed by n characters: 5HHELLO. Quotes came later and are much easier.
The control character can do more: 0 adds an empty line before the line, 1 starts a new page.

exercises.prompt: Where does the text of a printed line go?
options: On a separate card after END
exercises.explanation: WRITE lists values, the FORMAT holds the text.

exercises.prompt: What does / do in a FORMAT?
exercises.explanation: Inside a FORMAT, / means: this line is done, continue on the next.

options: The old way to write the text HELLO: H with the number of characters in front
exercises.explanation: Hollerith text, named after Herman Hollerith, inventor of the punch card. 5H says: the next 5 characters are text.
The text, then 7 right-aligned in I4.

exercises.prompt: Print the two lines on separate lines.
exercises.explanation: A slash starts a new line.
